title: Instacart handoff UX, attempt lifecycle and dogfood metrics
body:
## Role
A product engineer who makes the handoff honest in every channel.

## Goal
Present the Instacart link to OpenClaw and the web dashboard in accurate language, show what was sent and what still needs review, track the attempt's lifecycle, and keep the universal export one tap away.

## Context
Attempts and statuses come from #148; translation issues from #147. Dogfood protocol is backlog P1.17.

## Deliverables
- v2 API response for a handoff: link, `expires_at`, the line items as sent, and translation issues.
- Dashboard view of the plan's handoff with a "Review in Instacart" button and "Export list instead".
- Attempt states `created`, `opened` (when the user follows the link through our redirect, if #139 allows one), `expired`, `failed`.
- Metrics: handoffs created, corrected before handoff, abandoned (expired unopened), and later reconciled (#150).

## Concrete examples
- OpenClaw says: "Your plan is ready to review in Instacart. 2 items need your check: peanut-free isn't a filter Instacart supports, and the organic filter won't apply to the milk UPC."
- Never: "Ordered", "Your groceries are on the way", or any status implying purchase.

## Constraints
- No state reads as ordered, paid, or received.
- The universal export works whether or not Instacart is enabled or failing.
- Metrics carry no item names or household details beyond counts.

## Dependencies
#148, #136; #150 for the reconciled metric.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A copy test asserts banned words ("ordered", "purchased", "on the way") never appear in handoff responses or templates.
- [ ] Every attempt state renders, including `failed` with the export fallback.
- [ ] Metrics increment as documented.

## Testing requirements
Flask template tests, API response contract tests, metric unit tests.

## Out of scope
Receipt import, notifications beyond the existing channels.

## Documentation requirements
README OpenClaw section; the dogfood protocol notes what to record.

## Done-Done (repository requirements)
- Invoke tools through `./scripts/*`, never directly; `./scripts/check-all.sh` exits 0.
- Keep the repository's coverage, typing, lint, security and complexity thresholds; don't weaken any gate.
- No `noqa`, `type: ignore`, disabled checks, test skips or retries added to get green. A flaky test is worse than no test.
- Deterministic contract tests and negative-path tests. Tests use a fake transport; a normal test run never calls Instacart.
- Update the docs and API contracts this change touches in the same PR.
- Review the final diff for Safeway or Instacart coupling in core domain modules (`consolidator`, `pantry_manager`, `recipe_store`, `models`, `pending_actions`).
- The PR body references the epic (#142) and closes this issue.
